private_note: Middle fifth numbers: Cedar 76, Alder 72, Today 72, Birch 68, Hazel 64. Cedar is best for us, but it cuts the bottom two fifths, so it probably can't reach 9 votes. Alder matches today's income and adds a guaranteed floor and health coverage, which protects us if a job or health shock hits. Birch and Hazel cost us real money, so I'd rather the convention fail than adopt either.
statement: I teach elementary school, my partner is an apprentice electrician, and we're paying off a small house. We're the middle of this country, and I'll vote for the middle's interests. By the staff's numbers, Cedar is the only plan that raises our income, to 76 from 72, so that's my first choice today. I also know nine votes is a high bar. Alder keeps middle households exactly where we are now, guarantees everyone a minimum income and basic health coverage, and puts most of the cost on the top groups. I can support Alder. I can't support Birch or Hazel: they cut middle-fifth income to 68 and 64, and they shrink the average economy by about a fifth. Families like mine would pay for that. If the plan that wins has to be a compromise, I'd like it to be one that doesn't take from the middle.
